description: §4.12.5 + §23.4 — the CLAIMED half of the sidecar pair, and the DOUBLE-FIRE GUARD for the S356 r3 conditional carve-out. A nested `<program name="ml" lang="go" …>` whose parent DOES declare `use foreign:ml { predict }` is refused exactly once, by §23.4's E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL at the `use foreign:` site. E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL must NOT also fire: two errors on one unbuilt shape is two diagnostics for one mistake, and that carve-out is the ratified position. Its sibling `foreign-sidecar-no-worker` pins the other half — an UNCLAIMED sidecar, where there is no `use foreign:` to fire at, so the carve-out would suppress the ONLY diagnostic and the declaration would compile to exit 0 with its body silently discarded. Together the two cases pin the invariant as ONE-DIAGNOSTIC-PER-MISTAKE rather than as an unconditional exemption. Which CODES exist is unchanged by this pair; only the condition each fires on was made precise.
rationale: §4.12.3 normative: "Where an execution context's codegen is not implemented in a given compiler revision, that revision SHALL emit NEITHER a reference to the context … NOR an artifact standing in for it, and SHALL fail closed with a diagnostic naming the context (`E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL`, §4.12.9; or, for the §4.12.5 sidecar, the §23.4 `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` at the `use foreign:` site)." The "or" is the whole point: SPEC names TWO diagnostics for the sidecar and expects ONE of them, not both and not neither. This case pins the `use foreign:`-site branch; `foreign-sidecar-no-worker` pins the declaration-site branch that applies when the `use foreign:` does not exist.
